title: Acid derivatives
unit: A2 (inferred from organic chemistry content; unit number not stated in text)

questions.question: Which ester has 54.5% carbon by mass? Options: A methyl methanoate, B methyl ethanoate, C ethyl ethanoate, D ethyl methanoate.
steps: Only option C gives 54.5% carbon

questions.question: Give the systematic name for isoamyl acetate, an ester of ethanoic acid (CH3COOCH2CH2CH(CH3)2).
steps: Acid part CH3COO- is ethanoate (from ethanoic acid)
Alkyl part CH2CH2CH(CH3)2 is a 5-carbon chain with a methyl branch on C3
Name the alkyl group first: 3-methylbutyl, then ethanoate

questions.question: 6.06 x 10^-3 mol NaOH reacted with the ester in 1.07 g of banana flavouring. Find the percentage by mass of the ester (isoamyl acetate).
steps: Ester is C7H14O2, Mr = 130.2
Ester hydrolysis is 1:1, so moles of ester = moles of NaOH = 6.06 x 10^-3 mol
Mass of ester = 6.06 x 10^-3 x 130.2 = 0.789 g

questions.question: 25.0 cm^3 of 0.980 mol dm^-3 NaOH was used to hydrolyse the ester; 6.06 x 10^-3 mol of NaOH reacted with the ester. Find the pH of the mixture at completion, assuming total volume 25.0 cm^3. [Kw = 1.0 x 10^-14 mol2 dm-6]
steps: Moles NaOH initially = 0.980 x 0.0250 = 0.0245 mol
Ester hydrolysis uses NaOH 1:1, so NaOH left = 0.0245 - 0.00606 = 0.01844 mol
[OH-] = 0.01844 / 0.0250 = 0.738 mol dm^-3 (strong base, fully dissociated)

questions.question: Which student is correct about using methyl orange and/or phenolphthalein to titrate the excess NaOH (mixture also contains sodium ethanoate) with HCl? Student A: only methyl orange; B: only phenolphthalein; C: either.
questions.answer: Student B is correct: only phenolphthalein gives the right end point
steps: Titre should measure only the excess strong base NaOH
First end point (NaOH neutralised) is at about pH 9, inside the phenolphthalein range (8.3-10.0)
Methyl orange changes at pH 3.1-4.4, only reached after the ethanoate ion is also protonated
Using methyl orange would include the ethanoate, giving a titre that is too large
Students A and C are wrong

questions.question: Describe how the sodium ethanoate in the final reaction mixture could be converted into ethanoic acid.
questions.answer: Add dilute strong acid (e.g. HCl) to protonate the ethanoate, then distil off the ethanoic acid
steps: CH3COONa + HCl -> CH3COOH + NaCl
A strong acid protonates the weak-acid conjugate base ethanoate
Ethanoic acid (bp 118 deg C) is volatile enough to be separated from the salt solution by distillation

questions.question: Find the pH of the buffer made by mixing 50.0 cm^3 of 0.150 mol dm^-3 ethanoic acid with 30.0 cm^3 of 0.142 mol dm^-3 NaOH. [Ka for ethanoic acid = 1.70 x 10^-5 mol dm-3]
questions.answer: pH = 4.89 (Ka of ethanoic acid = 1.70 x 10^-5 mol dm^-3)
steps: Moles CH3COOH = 0.150 x 0.0500 = 7.50 x 10^-3 mol
NaOH reacts completely: CH3COOH + NaOH -> CH3COONa + H2O
Acid left = 7.50 - 4.26 = 3.24 x 10^-3 mol; salt CH3COONa formed = 4.26 x 10^-3 mol
pH = pKa + log(salt/acid) = 4.77 + log(4.26/3.24) = 4.77 + 0.12 = 4.89 (volumes cancel)

questions.question: Explain why small amounts of NaOH and HCl added to the buffer in (b)(i) cause little change in pH. Illustrate with at least two equations.
questions.answer: The buffer holds a large amount of weak acid (CH3COOH) and its conjugate base (CH3COO-), which remove added OH- and H+ so pH barely changes
steps: Buffer equilibrium: CH3COOH <=> CH3COO- + H+
Added NaOH: OH- + CH3COOH -> CH3COO- + H2O (OH- removed by the weak acid)
Added HCl: H+ + CH3COO- -> CH3COOH (H+ removed by the conjugate base)
Equilibrium shifts to replace the lost H+ (left or right, Le Chatelier)
Both species are present in large amounts, so the [acid]/[salt] ratio changes only slightly
pH = pKa + log([A-]/[HA]) therefore changes very little

questions.question: Which of four C5 compounds (options A-D, compounds 1-4), when mixed with water, gives the solution with lowest pH?
steps: Compound 1 is pentanoyl chloride, an acyl chloride. It reacts rapidly with water: CH3CH2CH2CH2COCl + H2O -> CH3CH2CH2CH2COOH + HCl.
The HCl produced is a strong acid and the carboxylic acid is also acidic, so the solution has a low pH.
The aldehyde (2), ketone (3) and amide (4) give essentially neutral solutions.

questions.question: Which of compounds 1-4 (options A-D) reacts with ethylamine, CH3CH2NH2, to form an N-substituted amide?
steps: An N-substituted amide is formed when a primary amine attacks an acyl chloride in a nucleophilic addition-elimination reaction.
CH3CH2CH2CH2COCl + 2CH3CH2NH2 -> CH3CH2CH2CH2CONHCH2CH3 + CH3CH2NH3+ Cl-.
The aldehyde, ketone and amide do not react with ethylamine in this way.

questions.question: Which of compounds 1-4 (options A-D) reacts with iodine and sodium hydroxide to give a pale yellow precipitate?
steps: The iodoform reaction (I2 with NaOH, giving pale yellow CHI3) needs a CH3C=O group (or CH3CH(OH)-).
Compound 3 is CH3COCH2CH2CH3, pentan-2-one, a methyl ketone, so it gives the pale yellow precipitate of triiodomethane.
Pentanal (2), the acyl chloride (1) and the amide (4) have no CH3C=O group.

questions.question: A polymer is made from hexanedioyl dichloride and hexane-1,6-diamine. What type of polymerisation occurs? Options: A addition, B condensation, C hydrolysis, D substitution.
steps: Amide links form between the acyl chloride and amine groups
A small molecule (HCl) is eliminated at each linkage
Loss of a small molecule when linking monomers means condensation polymerisation
Addition needs a C=C double bond; hydrolysis needs water to split a bond

questions.question: Which of the following could not be formed when methylamine is added to ethanoyl chloride? (Options A-D)
steps: Methylamine reacts with ethanoyl chloride by nucleophilic addition-elimination: CH3COCl + CH3NH2 -> CH3CONHCH3 + HCl, so D and A form.
The HCl formed reacts with more methylamine: CH3NH2 + HCl -> CH3NH3+ Cl-, so B forms.
CH3CONH2 (ethanamide) would need ammonia, not methylamine, so it cannot form.

questions.question: Butanoic acid may be prepared by acid hydrolysis of: A butyl ethanoate, B 1-chlorobutane, C ethyl butanoate, D propanenitrile.
steps: Acid hydrolysis of an ester gives the carboxylic acid plus alcohol
CH3CH2CH2COOC2H5 + H2O -> CH3CH2CH2COOH + C2H5OH
Butyl ethanoate gives ethanoic acid; propanenitrile gives propanoic acid
1-chlorobutane gives butan-1-ol, not an acid

questions.question: What speeds up the slow formation and hydrolysis of esters under normal laboratory conditions? (Options A-D)
questions.answer: B: acids only for esterification; acids and bases for hydrolysis
steps: Esterification of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol needs an acid catalyst (concentrated H2SO4). A base would convert the carboxylic acid to its salt, which does not esterify.
Hydrolysis of an ester is speeded up by dilute acid (a catalyst) and also by alkali such as NaOH (hydroxide ions attack the ester, giving the carboxylate salt and the alcohol).
So esterification: acids only; hydrolysis: acids and bases, which is B.

questions.question: Which reagent reacts at room temperature with methylamine to form N-methylethanamide? Options: A CH3COCH3, B CH3COOH, C CH3COOCH3, D CH3COCl.
steps: N-methylethanamide is CH3CONHCH3, formed by acylation of methylamine
Acyl chlorides react with amines rapidly at room temperature
Ethanoic acid only forms a salt with the amine at room temperature
Methyl ethanoate needs heating; propanone (ketone) does not acylate amines

questions.question: Which structure is the repeat unit of PHBV, a polymer formed from 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid?
steps: PHBV is a polyester, so the monomers join by ester links formed between the OH of one hydroxyacid and the COOH of the next, losing water.
The repeat unit must contain one unit from each monomer: -O-CH(CH3)-CH2-C(=O)- (from 3-hydroxybutanoic acid) and -O-CH(CH2CH3)-CH2-C(=O)- (from 3-hydroxypentanoic acid).
It must begin at an O and end at a C=O so that the repeating unit can join end to end with an ester link, giving B.
A ends in -O- as well as starting with -O-, which would give O-O links; C has no O at the start; D is not made from these monomers.

questions.question: What reaction occurs when PHBV biodegrades to its monomers? Options: A condensation, B hydrolysis, C hydration, D hydrogenation.
steps: PHBV is a polyester containing ester links
Biodegradation splits the ester links by reaction with water
Splitting a bond with water is hydrolysis; condensation is the reverse, joining monomers with loss of water

questions.question: Propyl ethanoate, CH3COOCH2CH2CH3, is hydrolysed with aqueous NaOH. Which products form? Options: A CH3COOH and CH3CH2CH2OH, B CH3COOH and CH3CH2CH2ONa, C CH3COONa and CH3CH2CH2OH, D CH3COONa and CH3CH2CH2ONa.
steps: Alkaline hydrolysis of an ester gives a carboxylate salt and an alcohol
CH3COOCH2CH2CH3 + NaOH -> CH3COONa + CH3CH2CH2OH
The acid is formed as its sodium salt, not free ethanoic acid, in NaOH

questions.question: Terylene is made from ethane-1,2-diol and terephthalic acid. Which structure is its repeat unit? (Options A-D)
steps: Terylene is made by condensation polymerisation of benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid with ethane-1,2-diol, forming ester links -C(=O)-O-CH2CH2-O-C(=O)-.
The repeat unit is -O-C(=O)-C6H4-C(=O)-O-CH2CH2- with the carbonyl carbons attached to the benzene ring.
In B, two CH2CH2 groups would be joined when repeated, giving a chain of four carbons. C and D have the O atoms attached to the ring, which is not what comes from the acid. A is correct.

questions.question: Which compound is completely miscible with water and has a higher boiling point than water? Options: A CH3COOH, B CH3COCH3, C CH3CH2CH2CHO, D CH3CH2COOCH2CH3.
steps: Ethanoic acid forms hydrogen bonds with water, so it is miscible
Its boiling point is 118 deg C, above water at 100 deg C
Acetone is miscible but boils at 56 deg C
Butanal (bp 76 deg C) and ethyl propanoate (bp 99 deg C, 5 carbons) are not miscible with water

questions.question: 0.200 mol ethanoic acid and 0.150 mol ethanol reach equilibrium at 25 deg C. The equilibrium mixture needs 34.8 cm^3 of 2.50 mol dm^-3 NaOH to neutralise its ethanoic acid. Calculate Kc.
steps: Moles of acid at equilibrium = 0.0348 x 2.50 = 0.0870 mol (1:1 with NaOH)
Ester and water formed = 0.200 - 0.0870 = 0.113 mol each
Ethanol at equilibrium = 0.150 - 0.113 = 0.0370 mol
Volume cancels (2 mol on each side), so Kc = 0.012769 / 0.003219 = 3.97

questions.question: Explain, using the types and numbers of bonds broken and made, why the enthalpy change for esterification is small.
questions.answer: The same number and types of bonds are broken (C-O and O-H) and made (C-O and O-H), so the energy changes nearly cancel
steps: RCOOH + R'OH -> RCOOR' + H2O
Bonds broken: one C-O and one O-H (from the acid and alcohol)
Bonds made: one C-O (ester) and one O-H (water)
Same types and numbers of bonds broken and made, so the enthalpy change is small

questions.question: Name the carboxylic acid, alcohol and catalyst used in Reaction 1 for making an ester that smells of raspberries.
questions.answer: Carboxylic acid: methanoic acid; alcohol: 2-methylpropan-1-ol; catalyst: concentrated sulfuric acid
steps: HCOOH is methanoic acid.
(CH3)2CHCH2OH is 2-methylpropan-1-ol.
The catalyst for esterification is a strong acid, concentrated sulfuric acid.

questions.question: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of Reaction 2 compared with Reaction 1 for making the raspberry ester.
questions.answer: Advantage: Reaction 2 goes to completion (irreversible), giving a higher yield. Disadvantage: methanoyl chloride is hazardous (it reacts violently with water and releases corrosive HCl gas) and more costly.
steps: Advantage: Reaction 1 is reversible and reaches equilibrium with only part of the reactants converted, whereas Reaction 2 is not reversible, so all of the reactants can be converted and the yield of ester is higher.
Another advantage: the acyl chloride reacts rapidly at room temperature without a catalyst or heating.
Disadvantage: methanoyl chloride is corrosive and reacts violently with water (moisture), so it must be handled under dry conditions.
The reaction also gives off HCl, a toxic, corrosive gas, and the acyl chloride must itself be made from the acid, which is an extra step and costs more.

questions.question: Which compound is a product of hydrolysing CH3COOC3H7 (ester formula partly garbled in text) with aqueous NaOH? Options: A CH3OH, B C3H7OH, C C3H7COOH, D C3H7COO-Na+.
steps: The ester is propyl ethanoate, CH3COO-C3H7
NaOH hydrolysis gives CH3COO-Na+ and C3H7OH
C3H7OH is the alcohol product
CH3OH, C3H7COOH and C3H7COO-Na+ are not products of this ester

questions.question: Compare and contrast the reactions of ethanoyl chloride with water, with ethanol and with ammonia. Refer to structural features, identify products and include equations as needed.
questions.answer: Water: CH3COOH + HCl; ethanol: CH3COOC2H5 + HCl; ammonia: CH3CONH2 + NH4Cl (2 mol NH3 needed)
steps: The C=O carbon bears a partial positive charge from O and Cl, so it is attacked by nucleophiles
Each reaction is addition-elimination with Cl- as the leaving group, giving HCl
Water (O lone pair) gives ethanoic acid: CH3COCl + H2O -> CH3COOH + HCl
Ethanol (O lone pair) gives an ester: CH3COCl + C2H5OH -> CH3COOC2H5 + HCl
Ammonia (N lone pair) gives an amide: CH3COCl + 2NH3 -> CH3CONH2 + NH4Cl
Ammonia needs two moles because the second NH3 neutralises the HCl; water and ethanol give HCl directly

questions.question: Which reaction does not produce a tertiary alcohol as one of the products? Options: A (CH3)2C=CH2 + H2O, B (CH3)3CBr + H2O, C (CH3)3CCOC(CH3)3 + LiAlH4, D (CH3)3CCOOC(CH3)3 + NaOH.
questions.answer: C - reduction of the ketone gives a secondary alcohol
steps: A: hydration of the alkene gives (CH3)3COH, a tertiary alcohol
B: hydrolysis of (CH3)3CBr gives (CH3)3COH, a tertiary alcohol
D: alkaline hydrolysis of the ester gives (CH3)3COH as the alcohol product
C: LiAlH4 reduces the ketone C=O to a CH-OH group, giving a secondary alcohol

questions.question: Which reaction cannot form a carboxylic acid? Options: A oxidation of a primary alcohol, B acidic hydrolysis of a nitrile, C alkaline hydrolysis of an ester, D acyl chloride reacting with water.
questions.answer: C - alkaline hydrolysis of an ester gives a carboxylate salt, not the free acid
steps: A: excess oxidant turns a primary alcohol into a carboxylic acid
B: acid hydrolysis of a nitrile gives the carboxylic acid and an ammonium salt
D: acyl chloride + water gives the carboxylic acid and HCl
C: NaOH gives the carboxylate salt (e.g. CH3COO-Na+) and alcohol; the free acid appears only after adding acid

questions.question: Which is produced after the polyester shown is hydrolysed with excess NaOH? Options: A benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid, B ethane-1,2-diol, C sodium ethanedioate, D water.
steps: The polyester is poly(ethylene terephthalate), joined by ester links -C(=O)-O-CH2CH2-O-.
Hot aqueous NaOH hydrolyses every ester link, giving the sodium salt of the dicarboxylic acid and the diol: ethane-1,2-diol.
Excess NaOH keeps the acid as its sodium salt, so A is not formed. Sodium ethanedioate (C) has the wrong carbon chain, and water is not a product of ester hydrolysis.

questions.question: How many curly arrows are needed to complete the mechanism of ethanoyl chloride with concentrated aqueous ammonia? Options: A 4, B 5, C 6, D 8.
steps: Step 1 needs 2 arrows: the N lone pair to the C, and the C=O pi bond to O (making O-).
Step 2 needs 2 arrows: a lone pair on O- back to the carbon to reform C=O, and the C-Cl bond to Cl (leaving as Cl-).
Step 3 needs 2 arrows: the lone pair on a second NH3 to the H of N+-H, and the N-H bond to the N (making the neutral amide and NH4+).
Total 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 curly arrows.

questions.question: What is the IUPAC name of the organic product of ethanoyl chloride with concentrated ammonia? Options: A amino ethanone, B ethanamide, C ethanoyl amine, D methanamide.
steps: Product is CH3CONH2, an amide with two carbons
Amides take the -amide ending from the -oic acid parent: ethanoic acid gives ethanamide
Amino ethanone is a ketone name; ethanoyl amine is not IUPAC; methanamide has one carbon

questions.question: Two monomers react to form a polymer. Which structure is a repeat unit of the polymer? (Options A-D)
steps: Monomer 1 is a diol with two OH groups and monomer 2 is a dicarboxylic acid, HOOC-C(CH3)2-COOH, so they make a polyester by condensation.
The repeat unit contains the full diol residue -O-CH2CH2-C(CH2CH3)2-CH2-O- joined by ester links to -C(=O)-C(CH3)2-C(=O)-.
B has a CH2OH group in place of an ethyl group, so it is not the same diol. C and D have ether links and a wrong structure.

questions.question: The structure of an ester is shown. Which two compounds react to form it? Options: A butanoyl chloride and 2-methylbutan-2-ol, B butanoyl chloride and 3-methylbutan-2-ol, C propanoyl chloride and 2-methylbutan-2-ol, D propanoyl chloride and 3-methylbutan-2-ol.
steps: The ester is CH3CH2CH2COOCH(CH3)CH(CH3)2. The acyl part, CH3CH2CH2C(=O)-, has four carbons, so it comes from butanoyl chloride.
The alkyl part, -CH(CH3)CH(CH3)2, comes from the alcohol (CH3)2CHCH(OH)CH3, with OH on carbon 2 and a methyl on carbon 3: 3-methylbutan-2-ol.
So butanoyl chloride and 3-methylbutan-2-ol react: B.

questions.question: Polyesters are made by reacting: A diprotic carboxylic acids with a primary alcohol, B diprotic carboxylic acids with diols, C monoprotic carboxylic acids with triols, D monoprotic carboxylic acids with a secondary alcohol.
questions.answer: B - diprotic carboxylic acids with diols
steps: Polyesters need two reactive groups on each monomer to build a chain
A diprotic acid has two -COOH groups; a diol has two -OH groups
Each ester link forms with loss of water (condensation)

questions.question: Why is the ester yield usually higher from an acyl chloride than from a carboxylic acid with an alcohol? Options: A acyl chlorides react to remove any water produced, B the reaction is not reversible, C the reaction is less exothermic, D the reaction has a higher atom economy.
questions.answer: B - the acyl chloride reaction is not reversible
steps: Esterification from a carboxylic acid is reversible and reaches an equilibrium
Acyl chloride + alcohol -> ester + HCl goes effectively to completion
Because the reaction does not reach equilibrium, the yield is higher

questions.question: Which reaction does not produce a carboxylic acid? Options: A acyl chloride with cold water, B ester refluxed with dilute HCl, C nitrile refluxed with aqueous KOH, D primary alcohol oxidised with excess acidified dichromate.
questions.answer: C - nitrile refluxed with aqueous KOH gives a potassium carboxylate salt
steps: A: acyl chloride + water gives the carboxylic acid and HCl
B: acid-catalysed ester hydrolysis gives the carboxylic acid and alcohol
D: excess acidified dichromate oxidises the primary alcohol to a carboxylic acid
C: alkaline hydrolysis gives the carboxylate salt (and NH3); the free acid needs a further acidification step

questions.question: What is the organic product of ethanoyl chloride reacting with ammonia gas? Options: A ammonium ethanoate, B ethanamide, C ethanenitrile, D methanenitrile.
steps: CH3COCl + 2NH3 -> CH3CONH2 + NH4Cl
The organic product is the amide ethanamide
Ammonium ethanoate is an ionic salt, not the organic product; nitriles are not formed

questions.question: 0.100 mol ethyl propanoate and 0.200 mol water with HCl catalyst reach equilibrium at 25 deg C; 0.0440 mol propanoic acid is present. Calculate Kc to an appropriate number of significant figures.
steps: Propanoic acid = ethanol at equilibrium = 0.0440 mol
Ester remaining = 0.100 - 0.0440 = 0.0560 mol
Water remaining = 0.200 - 0.0440 = 0.156 mol
Volume cancels (2 mol each side); Kc = 0.001936 / 0.008736 = 0.222 (3 s.f.)

questions.question: Explain, using bonds broken and made and without calculations, why the enthalpy change for ethyl propanoate hydrolysis is close to but not exactly zero.
questions.answer: Same types and numbers of bonds are broken (C-O, O-H) and made (C-O, O-H), so the enthalpy change is small but not exactly zero because bond strengths differ slightly
steps: Ester + water -> acid + alcohol
Bonds broken: one C-O (ester) and one O-H (water)
Bonds made: one C-O (acid) and one O-H (alcohol)
Same bond types and numbers, so bond energies nearly cancel
Bond strengths in different environments differ slightly, so the value is not exactly zero

questions.question: Deduce the effect of increasing temperature on the total entropy change and on Kc for the hydrolysis of ethyl propanoate. Assume the entropy change of the system does not change with temperature.
questions.answer: Delta S total stays almost the same, and Kc stays almost the same, because Delta H is close to zero
steps: Delta S total = Delta S system + Delta S surroundings, and Delta S surroundings = -Delta H / T.
Delta H is close to zero, so Delta S surroundings is close to zero at every temperature. Raising T makes it smaller still.
Delta S system is assumed constant, so Delta S total is essentially unchanged by increasing the temperature.
Since R ln K = Delta S total, Kc is also (almost) unchanged, so the equilibrium position hardly shifts.

questions.question: State the difference between a weak acid and a strong acid such as hydrochloric acid.
questions.answer: A strong acid is fully dissociated in water; a weak acid is only partly dissociated (an equilibrium)
steps: Strong acid: HCl -> H+ + Cl-, essentially complete dissociation
Weak acid: HA <=> H+ + A-, equilibrium lies well to the left
So at equal concentration a strong acid gives a much higher [H+]

questions.question: Calculate the pH of 0.500 mol dm^-3 hydrochloric acid at 25 deg C.
steps: HCl is fully dissociated, so [H+] = 0.500 mol dm^-3

questions.question: Calculate the pH of 0.500 mol dm^-3 propanoic acid at 25 deg C, given Ka = 1.30 x 10^-5 mol dm^-3.
steps: Ka = [H+]^2 / c, with [H+] = [A-] and c approximately [HA] (dissociation is small)

questions.question: Calculate the pH at the point in the titration of propanoic acid with NaOH where half the acid has been neutralised. Show working.
steps: At half neutralisation [HA] = [A-]
Henderson equation gives [H+] = Ka, so pH = pKa

questions.question: Sketch the titration curve for adding 50 cm^3 of 0.500 mol dm^-3 NaOH to 25.0 cm^3 of 0.500 mol dm^-3 propanoic acid, using answers to (b)(iii) and (c)(i).
questions.answer: Curve from pH 2.59 (0 cm^3), pH 4.89 (12.5 cm^3), equivalence pH 9.14 (25.0 cm^3), to pH 13.22 (50.0 cm^3)
steps: Start point at 0 cm^3 is pH 2.59 from (b)(iii)
Half-equivalence at 12.5 cm^3 is pH 4.89 from (c)(i)
Equivalence at 25.0 cm^3 (0.0125 mol each): propanoate 0.250 mol dm^-3 in 50.0 cm^3; Kb = Kw/Ka = 7.7 x 10^-10; [OH-] = sqrt(Kb x 0.250) = 1.39 x 10^-5; pH = 9.14
Curve rises steeply through the equivalence point
At 50.0 cm^3 excess NaOH = 0.0125 mol in 75.0 cm^3, [OH-] = 0.167 mol dm^-3, pH = 13.22, curve levels off at high pH

questions.question: Suggest a suitable indicator for the propanoic acid and NaOH titration, justifying the choice using the titration curve. Use the Data Booklet.
questions.answer: Phenolphthalein (pH range 8.3-10.0), because it changes colour within the steep part of the curve near pH 9.1
steps: Equivalence point is at pH 9.14, on the steep rise of the curve
Phenolphthalein changes colour over pH 8.3-10.0, which contains the equivalence point
Methyl orange (pH 3.1-4.4) changes around half neutralisation, long before the equivalence point, so it would give a wrong end point

questions.question: Which monomer could form a condensation polymer without needing a second type of monomer? (Options A-D)
steps: A condensation polymer from one monomer needs two different functional groups on the same molecule that can react together.
HO(CH2)4COCl has an OH group and a COCl (acyl chloride) group, so it can form ester links with itself (polyester), losing HCl.
A has two OH groups, C has OH and C=C, D has OH and an alkyl chloride; none of these has a pair of groups that react to give a condensation link.

questions.question: Ethanoyl chloride reacts with ammonia to form ethanamide. Which diagram shows the electron-pair movement when ethanamide forms from the tetrahedral intermediate?
steps: To form the amide, a lone pair on O- moves back to form the C=O: the arrow starts at the oxygen lone pair and points to the C-O bond.
The C-Cl bond breaks heterolytically: the arrow starts at the C-Cl bond and points to Cl, which leaves as Cl-.
The N+-H bond breaks, so the arrow starts at the N-H bond and points to the N, leaving H+ and a neutral N.
Only A has all three arrows in these directions. B has the C-Cl arrow reversed, C has the N-H arrow reversed and D has the O arrow reversed.

questions.question: CH3CH2COCl reacts with (1) CH3NH2 to give CH3CH2CONHCH3, (2) (CH3)2NH to give CH3CH2CON(CH3)2, (3) (CH3)3N to give CH3CH2CON(CH3)3. Which statements are correct? Options: A 1, 2 and 3; B 1 and 2 only; C 2 and 3 only; D 1 only.
steps: Statement 1: primary amine CH3NH2 gives an N-substituted amide, correct
Statement 2: secondary amine (CH3)2NH gives a tertiary amide, correct
Statement 3: tertiary amine (CH3)3N has no N-H and cannot form a neutral amide by substitution, so it is wrong

questions.question: An ester has the structure shown (diagram). Which pair of reactants forms it? Options: A butanoic acid and propan-2-ol, B butanoyl chloride and propan-1-ol, C propanoic acid and butan-1-ol, D propanoyl chloride and butan-2-ol.
steps: The acyl part, CH3CH2CH2C(=O)-, has four carbons, so the acid component is butanoic acid or butanoyl chloride.
The alkyl part on oxygen is CH2CH2CH3, a straight propyl chain attached through its end carbon, so the alcohol is propan-1-ol.
A would give the propan-2-yl ester. Options C and D use propanoyl (3 carbons) as the acyl part and so do not match.

questions.question: An ester is hydrolysed in excess dilute HCl to form ethanol and propanedioic acid. What is the skeletal formula of this ester? (Options shown as diagrams)
steps: Hydrolysis of the ester gives propanedioic acid, HOOCCH2COOH, plus ethanol, so the ester has two COO groups on a CH2, each joined to an ethyl group.
The ester is CH2(COOCH2CH3)2: the diester made of the dicarboxylic acid and two ethanol molecules.
B is propyl ethanoate, C is ethyl propanoate, and D is a diester of ethane-1,2-diol, which would give a different diol on hydrolysis.

questions.question: From which two reactants could CH3(CH2)2COO(CH2)4CH3 be made? Options: A butanoic acid and pentan-1-ol, B butanoyl chloride and butan-1-ol, C butanal and pentan-1-ol, D pentanoic acid and butan-1-ol.
steps: The ester is pentyl butanoate: acyl part from butanoic acid (4 C), alkyl part pentyl (5 C)
Butanoic acid and pentan-1-ol give the ester by esterification

questions.question: A polyester is made from pentane-1,5-diol and pentanedioic acid. Which is the repeat unit of this polyester? (Options shown as diagrams)
steps: Pentanedioic acid is HOOC-(CH2)3-COOH, so the acid part of the repeat unit is -C(=O)-(CH2)3-C(=O)-; pentane-1,5-diol is HO-(CH2)5-OH, giving -O-(CH2)5-O-.
The repeat unit must start with C=O and end with O so that it joins end to end with an ester link without O-O bonds: -C(=O)-(CH2)3-C(=O)-O-(CH2)5-O-.
A and B start with O and end with O, which would give O-O links when repeated; B and D use (CH2)5 in the acid part, which is wrong. C is correct.

questions.question: Which statement about the reaction of ethanoyl chloride with ammonia is not correct? Options: A an amide is formed, B the reaction is exothermic, C misty fumes and white smoke are given off, D a gas is produced that turns damp red litmus blue.
questions.answer: D - no alkaline gas is produced; ammonia is a reactant, and the products are the amide and NH4Cl
steps: A: CH3COCl + 2NH3 -> CH3CONH2 + NH4Cl, so an amide forms
B: the reaction is vigorous and releases heat, so it is exothermic
C: the HCl-related white smoke of NH4Cl is seen, consistent with the reaction
D: the products are an amide and a salt; no gas is produced, and ammonia (which turns damp red litmus blue) is consumed, not made
